subject: microbiology
title: Bacteriophage, Oncogenic Viruses, Prions, CJD and Kuru

steps.tx: A **bacteriophage** is a virus infecting bacteria. A typical tailed phage has an icosahedral head containing DNA, a contractile or noncontractile tail and tail fibres that recognise bacterial receptors. In the lytic cycle the phage replicates and lyses the host; in lysogeny its genome integrates as prophage or persists as plasmid and is copied with the cell. Phage choice determines toxin transfer and bacterial evolution.
steps.say: Phages are bacterial viruses that either lyse the host now or ride quietly as prophages.

left.title: Lytic cycle
points: Lysin breaks wall and progeny escape

right.title: Lysogenic cycle
points: Host may gain toxin or resistance traits
Induction can re enter lytic cycle

steps.tx: **Lysogenic conversion** explains several toxin genes: diphtheria toxin from corynephage beta, cholera toxin from CTX phi, some botulinum toxins, Shiga toxin from lambdoid phages and streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxins. A bacterium's virulence can therefore be a mobile phage property rather than a fixed species trait. Phage typing also historically tracked Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella outbreaks before whole genome sequencing.
steps.say: Some of microbiology's most famous toxins are phage genes expressed by their bacterial hosts.

right.title: Practical consequences
points: Toxin production can vary among strains
Antibiotics may induce some toxin phages
Genome sequencing now traces mobile elements precisely

steps.tx: **Oncogenic viruses** transform cells by viral oncoproteins, insertional activation or chronic inflammation. HPV E6 and E7 disable p53 and Rb; EBV latency proteins drive B cell proliferation; HBV and HCV cause hepatocellular carcinoma through integration, viral proteins and chronic injury; HHV 8 drives Kaposi sarcoma in immunosuppression. Vaccination against HPV and HBV prevents virus associated cancers upstream.
steps.say: Viral cancer prevention works best before infection, through HPV and hepatitis B vaccination.

left.title: Direct mechanisms
points: HTLV 1 Tax drives T cell proliferation
EBV latent proteins mimic growth signals

right.title: Indirect mechanisms
points: HBV and HCV chronic hepatic inflammation
Coinfections and aflatoxin can amplify liver risk

steps.tx: **Prions** are infectious proteins, not viruses. Normal prion protein PrP C converts into misfolded protease resistant PrP Sc, which templates further conversion and aggregates in brain. There is no nucleic acid genome, no useful routine culture or antibody response in the host, and infectivity resists many ordinary decontamination methods. Disease is transmissible, hereditary or sporadic depending on how the first misfolded seed arises.
steps.say: Prions transmit a shape, not a genome, and standard sterilisation assumptions fail.

right.title: Disease protein
points: PrP Sc rich in beta sheets
No nucleic acid has been identified as genome

steps.tx: **Creutzfeldt Jakob disease** occurs most often sporadically with rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, ataxia and characteristic MRI or EEG changes. Variant CJD followed bovine spongiform encephalopathy exposure, affects younger patients, begins often with psychiatric symptoms and involves lymphoreticular tissues more prominently. Genetic prion diseases include Gerstmann Straussler Scheinker syndrome and fatal familial insomnia from PRNP variants.
steps.say: Rapid dementia with myoclonus demands prion disease in the differential and urgent neurology input.

left.title: Sporadic CJD
points: MRI basal ganglia or cortical ribboning

right.title: Variant CJD
points: Linked to BSE contaminated food chain historically

steps.tx: **Kuru** was a prion disease transmitted among the Fore people of Papua New Guinea through ritual endocannibalism, especially consumption of brain tissue. It caused tremor, ataxia and progressive neurologic death and declined after the practice stopped, followed by very long incubation cases. Kuru provided decisive epidemiologic evidence that a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy could spread without a conventional microorganism.
steps.say: Kuru disappeared after transmission practice ceased, despite incubation periods lasting decades.
